items.title: Michael Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 22, 2021
items.q: It’s no accident that John Coltrane developed as he did. Well first of all he was a practice-a-holic even when the gig was over he had the horn out.

ctx.x: Is there any preparation that you do before the gig that may assist you in getting to that point where you want to be before you play?

There probably is you know. I haven’t been very methodical about that but I’m sure, you know for example people who meditate regularly have a certain discipline, develop a discipline to put them in a certain frame of mind before they do what they have to do. I could probably count on one hand the times when I reached like what seemed like an optimal state of mind when improvising was almost an out of body experience. I think playing every night, I mean it’s very hard to reach those states of mind when you’re…

Do you recall if those rare moments where all that came together were in a trio context or solo piano context? My reason for asking that is I’m wondering, the people that you play with over the years, have you made note of bassists and drummers who are the best helpers for you to enter that comfort zone?
